--- title: "Converting from polars to pandas dataframe is as easy as 1, 2, 3" subtitle: "to_pandas" author: '{{< var author >}}' date: '2025-10-05' date-format: iso toc: true toc-title: 'Sections' toc-location: right toc-depth: 3 categories: [100DaysOfPolars] --- Almost anything you can do in Pandas can also be done in Polars. However, there are certain outputs that are unique to Pandas, such as creating a hierarchical column table. Fortunately, converting a Polars dataframe to a Pandas dataframe is very easy. Below is a Polars dataframe showing some popular clothing brands. ::: {#b2faf6ce .cell execution_count=1} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
shape: (4, 3)
BrandCategoryPrice
strstri64
"Gucci""Premium"1000
"Versace""Premium"5000
"Forever21""Basic"39
"Gap""Basic"56
``` ::: ::: ## Change to pandas dataframe Suppose you want to pivot your data to create a hierarchical column table where *Category* is at the top, followed by *Brand*. Currently, this cannot be done in Polars. However, you can use the `to_pandas` method to convert your Polars dataframe into a Pandas dataframe. From there, you can pivot the data to achieve the desired output as shown below: ::: {#ad1fc5f6 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} (df .to_pandas() .pivot(columns=['Category', 'Brand'], values='Price') ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
Category Premium Basic
Brand Gucci Versace Forever21 Gap
0 1000.0 NaN NaN NaN
1 NaN 5000.0 NaN NaN
2 NaN NaN 39.0 NaN
3 NaN NaN NaN 56.0
``` ::: ::: Sign up for my {{< var polars_course >}} to learn more.
